title: Getting started with svines
text: S-vine model combines marginal distributions stationary vine copula. package exposes two layers separately: svine() fits complete distribution model observed data. estimates marginal distributions, transforms observations unit hypercube, fits copula. svinecop() fits copula therefore expects approximately uniform pseudo-observations. svine_dist() svinecop_dist() construct models specified margins, pair copulas, S-vine structure. argument p Markov order. order-one model relates current observation previous observation, larger values include additional lags.

title: Getting started with svines
text: returns data contain daily log returns 20 companies. use two series restrict candidate families keep example short. fitted object contains marginal models fit$margins copula model fit$copula. Standard rvinecopulib methods can applied copula component.
code: data(returns) x <- returns[1:200, 1:2]  fit <- svine(   x,   p = 1,   margin_families = c("norm", "std"),   family_set = c("gaussian", "t") ) fit #> 2-dimensional S-vine distribution model of order p = 1 ('svine_dist') summary(fit) #> $margins #> # A data.frame: 2 x 5  #>  margin    name     model             parameters loglik #>       1 Allianz    Normal       0.00034, 0.01536    551 #>       2     AXA Student-t 0.0019, 0.0197, 4.0004    522 #>  #> $copula #> # A data.frame: 5 x 10  #>  tree edge conditioned conditioning var_types   family rotation    parameters #>     1    1        3, 1                    c,c        t        0 -0.084, 4.781 #>     1    2        2, 1                    c,c        t        0    0.84, 4.87 #>     2    1        4, 1            3       c,c gaussian        0        -0.064 #>     2    2        3, 2            1       c,c gaussian        0         0.074 #>     3    1        4, 2         1, 3       c,c gaussian        0        -0.072 #>  df    tau #>   2 -0.054 #>   2  0.637 #>   1 -0.041 #>   1  0.047 #>   1 -0.046

title: Getting started with svines
text: Without conditioning history, svine_sim() generates new stationary time series. Supplying past instead generates paths conditional observed history. Pseudo-residuals conditional Rosenblatt transforms. fitted model order p, result NROW(x) - p rows.
code: sim <- svine_sim(n = 100, rep = 1, model = fit) dim(sim) #> [1] 100   2  next_obs <- svine_sim(n = 1, rep = 100, model = fit, past = x) dim(next_obs) #>     dim      #>   1   2 100 residuals <- svine_pseudo_residuals(x, fit) dim(residuals) #> [1] 199   2

title: Getting started with svines
text: discrete variables, specify var_types = "d" restrict margin_families suitable discrete families. following model uses two Poisson margins. svine() evaluates CDF, F(x), left limit, F(x-), constructs copula data automatically. calling svinecop() directly, supply regular CDF columns first, followed one left-limit column discrete variable.
code: counts <- cbind(   claims = rpois(250, lambda = 2),   events = rpois(250, lambda = 4) )  fit_discrete <- svine(   counts,   p = 1,   var_types = c("d", "d"),   margin_families = "pois",   family_set = "gaussian" ) fit_discrete #> 2-dimensional S-vine distribution model of order p = 1 ('svine_dist') svine_sim(5, rep = 1, model = fit_discrete) #>      claims events #> [1,]      2      5 #> [2,]      0      1 #> [3,]      5      5 #> [4,]      6      7 #> [5,]      2      3

title: Getting started with svines
text: marginal transformation handled separately, fit copula layer directly. Use svinecop_loglik(), svinecop_scores(), svinecop_hessian() copula-level inference. corresponding svine_* functions include marginal parameters.
code: u <- pseudo_obs(x) copula_fit <- svinecop(   u,   p = 1,   family_set = c("gaussian", "t") ) copula_fit #> 2-dimensional S-vine copula model of order p = 1 ('svinecop_dist')

text: R package provides functionality fit simulate stationary vine copula models time series. package built top rvinecopulib univariateML.

title: Stationary Vine Copula Models
text: Install released version CRAN. Install development version GitHub remotes.
code: install.packages("svines") # install.packages("remotes") remotes::install_github("tnagler/svines")

title: Stationary Vine Copula Models
text: detailed documentation examples, see package website. Use svine() observed data: estimates marginal distributions S-vine copula. Use svinecop() margins already transformed approximately uniform pseudo-observations.
code: library(svines) data(returns)  # data set of stock returns returns <- returns[1:500, 1:2]

title: Stationary Vine Copula Models
code: fit <- svine(returns, p = 1)  # Markov order 1 summary(fit) #> $margins #> # A data.frame: 2 x 5  #>  margin    name          model                         parameters loglik #>       1 Allianz Skew Student-t 0.00039, 0.01589, 5.45534, 0.91785   1382 #>       2     AXA Skew Student-t 0.00052, 0.02089, 4.35198, 0.90611   1260 #>  #> $copula #> # A data.frame: 5 x 10  #>  tree edge conditioned conditioning var_types family rotation   parameters df #>     1    1        3, 2                    c,c      t        0 0.037, 4.893  2 #>     1    2        2, 1                    c,c      t        0   0.86, 3.48  2 #>     2    1        4, 2            3       c,c    joe       90          1.1  1 #>     2    2        3, 1            2       c,c  indep        0               0 #>     3    1        4, 1         2, 3       c,c      t        0 0.079, 8.994  2 #>     tau #>   0.023 #>   0.662 #>  -0.033 #>   0.000 #>   0.051 contour(fit$copula)

title: Stationary Vine Copula Models
text: svine_sim() can used two different ways:

what: Generate a new time series of length 500
title: Stationary Vine Copula Models
code: sim <- svine_sim(n = 500, rep = 1, model = fit) pairs(sim) pairs(returns)

what: Sample conditionally on the observed past
title: Stationary Vine Copula Models
code: sim <- svine_sim(n = 1, rep = 100, model = fit, past = returns) pairs(t(sim[1, , ]))

title: Stationary Vine Copula Models
text: generate bootstrap replicates one-step block multiplier bootstrap, use
code: set.seed(2026) models <- svine_bootstrap_models(2, fit) summary(models[[1]]) #> $margins #> # A data.frame: 2 x 5  #>  margin    name          model                         parameters loglik #>       1 Allianz Skew Student-t 0.00057, 0.01437, 7.22824, 0.97850     NA #>       2     AXA Skew Student-t 0.00065, 0.01842, 5.29395, 0.98127     NA #>  #> $copula #> # A data.frame: 5 x 10  #>  tree edge conditioned conditioning var_types family rotation    parameters df #>     1    1        3, 2                    c,c      t        0 -0.022, 5.380  2 #>     1    2        2, 1                    c,c      t        0    0.84, 2.99  2 #>     2    1        4, 2            3       c,c    joe       90             1  1 #>     2    2        3, 1            2       c,c  indep        0                0 #>     3    1        4, 1         2, 3       c,c      t        0    0.11, 6.83  2 #>     tau #>  -0.014 #>   0.634 #>  -0.008 #>   0.000 #>   0.068

title: Stationary Vine Copula Models
text: Declare discrete variables var_types restrict marginal families suitable discrete distributions. following model uses Poisson margins Gaussian pair-copula family. svine() constructs required CDF left-limit CDF values automatically. Users calling svinecop() directly must supply regular F(x) columns, followed one F(x-) column discrete variable.
code: counts <- cbind(   claims = rpois(250, lambda = 2),   events = rpois(250, lambda = 4) ) fit_discrete <- svine(   counts,   p = 1,   var_types = c("d", "d"),   margin_families = "pois",   family_set = "gaussian" ) fit_discrete #> 2-dimensional S-vine distribution model of order p = 1 ('svine_dist') svine_sim(5, rep = 1, model = fit_discrete) #>      claims events #> [1,]      3      4 #> [2,]      0      5 #> [3,]      0      1 #> [4,]      3      5 #> [5,]      1      1

text: data matrix data.frame data. p Markov order. var_types variable types; character vector one entry per variable: "c" continuous, "d" discrete. Use "empirical" empirical CDFs. selcrit criterion family selection, either "loglik", "aic", "bic", "mbicv". ... arguments passed svinecop().

code: ## marginal objects # create dummy univariateML models univ1 <- univ2 <- univariateML::mlnorm(rnorm(10))  # modify the parameters to N(5, 10) and N(0, 2) distributions univ1[] <- c(5, 10) univ2[] <- c(0, 2)  ## copula object cs_struct <- cvine_structure(1:2) pcs <- list(   list(  # first tree     bicop_dist("clayton", 0, 3), # cross sectional copula     bicop_dist("gaussian", 0, -0.1)  # serial copula   ),   list(  # second tree     bicop_dist("gaussian", 0, 0.2), bicop_dist("indep")     ),   list( # third tree     bicop_dist("indep")   ) )  cop <- svinecop_dist(   pcs, cs_struct, p = 1, out_vertices = 1:2, in_vertices = 1:2)      model <- svine_dist(margins = list(univ1, univ2), copula = cop) summary(model) #> $margins #> # A data.frame: 2 x 5  #>  margin name  model parameters loglik #>       1   V1 Normal      5, 10    -16 #>       2   V2 Normal       0, 2    -16 #>  #> $copula #> # A data.frame: 5 x 10  #>  tree edge conditioned conditioning var_types   family rotation parameters df #>     1    1        3, 1                    c,c gaussian        0       -0.1  1 #>     1    2        2, 1                    c,c  clayton        0          3  1 #>     2    1        4, 1            3       c,c gaussian        0        0.2  1 #>     2    2        3, 2            1       c,c    indep        0             0 #>     3    1        4, 2         1, 3       c,c    indep        0             0 #>     tau #>  -0.064 #>   0.600 #>   0.128 #>   0.000 #>   0.000 #>

title: Stationary vine copula models — svinecop
text: data matrix data.frame pseudo-observations (approximately uniform margins). discrete variables declared var_types, append one left-limit column F(x-) per discrete variable regular columns. Use svine() handle transformation automatically. p Markov order. var_types variable types; character vector one entry per variable: "c" continuous, "d" discrete. Omitting var_types cs_structure provided silently fit continuous model. family_set character vector families; see rvinecopulib::bicop() additional options. cs_structure cross-sectional vine structure (see rvinecopulib::rvine_structure()); cs_structure = NA performs automatic structure selection. out_vertices permutation 1, ..., d specifying -vertices. selected automatically structure provided. fixed cs_structure requires explicit out_vertices in_vertices. in_vertices permutation 1, ..., d specifying -vertices. selected automatically structure provided. fixed cs_structure requires explicit out_vertices in_vertices. type type stationary vine; "S" (default) general S-vines, "D" Smith's long D-vine, "M" Beare Seo's M-vine. par_method estimation method parametric models, either "mle" sequential maximum likelihood, "itau" inversion Kendall's tau (available one-parameter families "t"). nonpar_method estimation method nonparametric models, either "constant" standard transformation estimator, "linear"/"quadratic" local-likelihood approximations order one/two. mult multiplier smoothing parameters nonparametric families. Values larger 1 make estimate smooth, values less 1 less smooth. selcrit criterion family selection, either "loglik", "aic", "bic", "mbic", "mbicv". weights optional vector weights observation. psi0 prior probability non-independence copula (used selcrit = "mbic" selcrit = "mbicv"). presel whether family set thinned according symmetry characteristics data. trunc_lvl truncation level. Inf, corresponding truncation, currently supported. tree_crit criterion tree selection, one "tau", "rho", "hoeffd", "mcor" Kendall's \(\tau\), Spearman's \(\rho\), Hoeffding's \(D\), maximum correlation, respectively. threshold thresholded vine copulas; NA indicates threshold selected automatically rvinecopulib::mBICV(). keep_data whether data stored (necessary using fitted()). show_trace logical; whether trace fitting progress printed. cores number cores use; 1, estimation pair copulas within tree done parallel.
